text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer says no longer prepared to compromise on health reform, says internal disagreement in coalition over health reforms also endangers other reform plans of government.

- Despite record unemployment in January of 4.6 million, Economics Minister Guenter Rexrod still sees positive outlook for economy and remains confident that unemployment will be lower by the end of the year.
- Berlin Senate calls the shooting and injuring of a bookshop owner by probable right-wing extremists a cowardly murder attempt.
- Young people aged 16 and above granted right to vote in the municipal elections in the state of Schleswig-Holstein.

- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) name members of delegation due to discuss tax reform plans with ruling coalition on Monday, including party leader Oskar Lafontaine and parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping.
- M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of 11.7 percent and the Bundesbank keeps interest rates unchanged.
- Opposition want post office to keep its monopoly, saying planned introduction of competition would cost tens of thousands of jobs and lead to a decline in the service.
HANDELSBLATT
- DAX index of 30 leading shares falls under 3,200 points as the dollar loses some ground.
- Dresdner Bank AG raises dividend for 1996 to 1.45 marks from 1.35 marks.
- Recovery in car orders in Germany has stalled, with manufacturers reporting nine percent fewer orders in January than the previous month.
- Association of mortgage banks says mortgage interest rates have reached a low point and are unlikely to fall anymore this year.
- Finance Minster Theo Waigel announces a concerted action for jobs and growth.
- Adam Opel AG, a unit of General Motors Corp and Volkswagen AG resume some production as Spanish truckers' strike ends.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Government and SPD say they will work together to fight mass unemployment dispite all their differences over economic policy.
- Ruling coalition wants to give up plans to protect the honour of soldiers by law.
- Group of parliament members want to stop new spelling laws.
- An arrested Iranian journalist whose fate is worrying the Bonn government has telephoned his wife in Germany to say he is well, but that he expects to be convicted.
- Magdeburg police detain two right-wing youths suspected of murdering a 17-year-old punk.
DIE WELT
- Waigel wants concerted action for growth and positions of ruling coalition and SPD seem to be getting closer ahead of tax reform talks on Monday.
- Resistance in parliament to new spelling laws.
- Lower Saxony interior minister Gerhard Glogowski says nuclear waste should be stored at the power plants that produced it.
- Arrest warrant issued against a teenager in case of violent murder of 17-year-old punk.
